title: Analytic Qubit Separation between POVMs and Projective Measurements
authors: Lin Zhu, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang
abstract: Generalized measurements can be implemented projectively after enlarging the Hilbert space, but this dilation changes the available local dimension. We construct a Bell functional with rational coefficients that separates the two measurement models at local dimension two. An explicit three-outcome qubit positive-operator-valued measure with rational matrix entries attains $2\sqrt2+1/100$. On the other hand, all qubit-projective strategies are bounded by $2\sqrt2+\sqrt5/250+\sqrt2/32400$, giving a fully analytic certified gap greater than $1/1000$. To our knowledge, this is the first fully analytic Bell-functional separation between qubit POVMs and qubit projective measurements over arbitrary shared two-qubit states. Lean certificate for the separation theorem is provided for completeness. Separately, an exact level-3 noncommutative sum-of-squares certificate proves that the explicit qubit strategy attains the unrestricted finite-dimensional tensor-product quantum optimum.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that general Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) can achieve correlations strictly greater than those achievable by projective measurements (PVMs) when local dimensions are fixed. The separation is quantified using a novel Bell functional and proven analytically via advanced algebraic techniques, establishing a fundamental resource difference in quantum measurement theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a rigorous, analytic separation between correlations achievable by general quantum measurements (POVMs) and those restricted to projective measurements (PVMs) in a bipartite setting.
main_result: An explicit qubit POVM was constructed whose Bell value strictly exceeds the upper bound derived for all possible qubit PVM strategies over arbitrary shared two-qubit states, establishing a certified gap greater than 1/1000.
method: The separation is formalized using a specialized Bell functional and proven analytically through advanced mathematical techniques, including the use of exact level-3 noncommutative sum-of-squares (SOS) certificates in an algebraic framework.
model_or_system: The study analyzes correlations in a finite bipartite setting involving shared two-qubit states ($ho_{AB}$), comparing measurement outcomes from general POVMs versus restricted PVMs on qubits.
key_observables: Bell functional value $B$, the quantum maximum $\Omega = 2\sqrt{2} + 1/100$, and the upper bound for qubit PVM strategies.
important_parameters: Local dimension (fixed vs. unrestricted), the small parameter $\epsilon$ used in constructing the separating functional, and the specific structure of the two-qubit state.
main_assumptions: The separation is only meaningful when local dimensions are constrained; otherwise, Naimark's theorem allows dilation to remove the distinction.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Bell scenario comparing qubit POVMs vs. qubit projective measurements using a specific functional $B$, and Table I summarizes benchmark values for different measurement types.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (POVM vs PVM separation) to constructing an explicit separating POVM, deriving the necessary algebraic bounds via SOS certificates, and finally proving that this constructed value attains the dimension-unrestricted quantum optimum.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly rigorous mathematical tool—an analytic Bell functional with an exact certificate—to quantify fundamental differences between measurement models in quantum information theory, which is crucial for understanding device capabilities.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Bell scenario for comparing qubit POVMs with qubit projective measurements. A source distributes a two-qubit state ρAB to Alice and Bob. Alice receives x ∈{0, 1, 2}, where x = 0, 1 label binary measurements and x = 2 labels a ternary measurement. Bob receives y ∈{0, 1} and performs a binary measurement. Their outputs determine conditional probabili- ties P(a, b | x, y), which are evaluated by the Bell functional B. In the separating strategy, Alice’s ternary measurement is a genuine qubit POVM, whereas every measurement in the fixed-qubit comparison class is projective.
